title: Conduct maintenance of seed testing equipment

lessons.title: Why equipment maintenance matters
lessons.html:
Why equipment maintenance matters

Seed test results are only as good as the equipment used. A balance that weighs wrongly, a germinator that runs too hot or a blocked divider gives wrong results. A wrong germination figure on a label can lead to a farmer planting poor seed, or to good seed being thrown away. Routine maintenance keeps equipment accurate and safe.

Common equipment in a seed laboratory

EquipmentWhat can go wrong
Analytical and top-loading balancesDrift, dirt in the pan, not level
Sample dividersSeed stuck in channels, uneven division
Germinators and germination roomsWrong temperature, faulty lights, dirty and mouldy
Drying ovensTemperature not stable
Moisture metersOut of calibration
GrindersBlunt blades, residue from previous sample
Seed counters and blowersBlocked, wrong settings
Refrigerators and cold roomsTemperature too high

Types of maintenance

  • Daily care: cleaning after use, visual checks, recording temperatures.
  • Routine checks: balance checks with test weights, thermometer checks, moisture meter checks against the oven method.
  • Planned maintenance: servicing and calibration by the supplier or an accredited calibration service, at set intervals.
  • Repairs: when something breaks, reported and done by qualified people.

The laboratory keeps a maintenance schedule and a record for each item, often with an equipment number on a sticker.

Laboratories that are accredited, or that test seed for certification, are audited. Auditors check that every item used for a test result was within its calibration date and that routine checks were done and recorded. A missing record can mean that results produced with that equipment are questioned, even if the equipment was actually working well. Maintenance is therefore part of quality, not an extra job.

lessons.title: Doing the maintenance and keeping records
lessons.html:
Doing the maintenance and keeping records

Cleaning

  • Balances: switch off, brush out the pan and chamber with a soft brush, wipe with a slightly damp cloth. Never pour liquid on a balance.
  • Dividers: brush and blow out all channels after every sample, so no seed is carried to the next.
  • Germinators: remove trays, wash and disinfect shelves and walls as the laboratory procedure says, check drains and water trays.
  • Grinders: unplug before cleaning, then brush out all residue.
  • Ovens: remove spilt seed and dust when cool.

Checks

  1. Balance check: level the balance using its bubble, zero it, place a certified test weight and compare the reading with the allowed limit in your procedure. Record the result.
  2. Temperature check: place a calibrated thermometer or data logger in the germinator or oven, compare with the display, and record.
  3. Moisture meter: compare readings on samples tested by the oven method, as procedure requires.

When something is wrong

  • Stop using the equipment.
  • Put an 'out of use' tag on it.
  • Report to your supervisor and record the fault.
  • Tell the supervisor which tests may have been affected since the last good check, so they can be reviewed.

Safety

Unplug electrical equipment before cleaning. Do not open electrical panels; leave repairs to qualified technicians. Wear gloves when cleaning equipment used for treated seed. Let ovens cool before cleaning.

Records

Record date, equipment number, task done, results of checks, and your name. Records show auditors that results are reliable.

Key points

  • Accurate results need clean, checked and calibrated equipment.
  • Clean dividers and grinders after every sample to avoid carry-over.
  • Check balances with test weights and temperatures with calibrated thermometers.
  • Tag faulty equipment out of use and report it.
  • Record every maintenance task and check.
